4.label: Symptom and root
4.text: Suppressing a crisis leaves its cause in place, and an organisation that treats the end of one disruption as stability will be caught off guard by the next. Diagnose and resolve the root condition; putting down the symptom only sets the timer on its recurrence.

5.label: Looking at the source
5.text: Organisations that look away from what went wrong delay the examination until the cost is higher. Look directly at what is causing the damage and stop managing the distance from it.

6.label: Decision Paralysis
6.text: Prolonged indecision is itself a decision, usually the worst one, because it commits resources to neither path while the cost of waiting compounds. At the decisive moment, force the choice into the open.

6.label: Kinetic Misalignment
6.text: When the priority is wrong, maximum effort produces minimum return: the activity is genuine, the energy is real and the output stays below what the input should produce. Fix the priority before improving the effort.

7.label: 01 · Structural Misfit
7.text: Many failures in growing organisations are failures of structural readiness: the team has scaled past its systems and the work has outgrown its structures. Find one process that no longer fits the volume, a meeting cadence that no longer serves the work or a reporting line that has become a bottleneck, and replace it.

7.label: 03 · Decision Bottlenecks
7.text: The single leader who handles everything because no one else is appointed to handle anything is one of the most common and costly organisational design failures. Structure the work so each matter is handled at the appropriate level.

9.label: Resistance is predictable
9.text: The first response to significant change is almost always resistance and escalation, and intensifying friction can be evidence that the direction is right. Plan for the first phase of resistance before launching the change.

9.label: A structural problem
9.text: Leaders caught between what they know is right and what their environment allows must address the environment as well as the decision. The problem is structural.

10.label: Early Identification
10.text: Confident diagnosis from incomplete data is a common failure. Distinguish present difficulty from final outcome.

10.label: Accurate Classification
10.text: Misdiagnosis leads to wrong action. Challenge the assumptions behind a diagnosis before choosing the intervention.

11.label: 02 · Streamline
11.text: Drift sets in when accumulated processes, activities and traditions become more important than the value they were meant to serve. Protect the core from the additions that obscure it.

11.label: 04 · Upgrade
11.text: Leaders who remain at the centre of every decision create dependency, slow decision-making and limited growth in others. Place responsibility close to the people who hold the knowledge and authority to carry it.

11.label: Mechanisms for action
11.text: Organisations often stay frustrated because they announce priorities without creating the mechanisms through which people can act on them. A practical mechanism converts intention into measurable progress.

15.label: Owning inherited problems
15.text: Leaders who own only what they personally initiated leave inherited breaches to fester. Accept the full liabilities of the position: the authority to fix a problem comes with the willingness to be accountable for it.

15.label: Self-generated dysfunction
15.text: Organisations are more effective at dismantling inherited problems than at confronting the ones current leadership has grown comfortable with. A complete audit asks what the current leadership is leaving in place.

17.label: Surfacing early
17.text: Naming a hidden problem specifically restores the capacity for forward movement. Build the conditions in which hidden problems can surface safely and early, before they surface at the worst possible moment.

17.label: The arithmetic of the cover-up
17.text: Every resource spent hiding a problem compounds its eventual cost. Make it cheaper to disclose than to hide, and model disclosure yourself; the leader who covers teaches everyone below to cover too.

21.label: Bring the plan
21.text: Leaders who present an immediately actionable response alongside the problem get the room and keep it. If you bring a diagnosis, bring a plan. Use this with Q4.

21.label: Act on what you know
21.text: When the usual signals go quiet, the instinct is to commission new intelligence. List the conclusions already reached and not acted on, and execute one.

22.label: Testing the intervention
22.text: Test whether an intervention is helping or adding burden. Execution depends on coordinated diversity of roles.

23.label: 02 · Clog and symptom
23.text: Persistent problems survive because the assumptions, beliefs and patterns producing them have never been challenged. Effective strategy addresses the root logic beneath the recurring symptoms.

23.label: Honest assessment first
23.text: Meaningful change starts with honest assessment, thoughtful preparation and patient execution, and it addresses root causes. Enduring change reshapes values and behaviours as well as processes.

24.label: Commitment to application
24.text: Organisations often receive a diagnosis, appreciate its quality and return to unchanged practice. Ask in advance: what will we do differently as a result of what we hear? Use this to test each commitment.

25.label: Old breaches
25.text: Some present problems are the bill for a past breach. When a recurring problem resists treatment, investigate what older, unsettled matter it may be surfacing.

25.label: Stepping over
25.text: A dangerous cultural failure is high-performing indifference: people who step over a problem every day without registering it as theirs to solve. Put it on the agenda before the stepping-over becomes the culture.
